title: regionwise-gpu-signal-and-rollout-timeline-experiment
content:
Purpose and context:

This is an experimental planning note that describes a signal-driven, regionwise capacity forecast and a lightweight rollout timeline for the next three quarters. The goal is to move away from monolithic monthly forecasts toward a cadence that reacts to live signals (latency SLO slippage, queue depth, committed reserved-usage delta) and stages GPU activation in short pulse windows to preserve budget flexibility.

Key ideas (short):
- Signal-based staging: define 3 operational signals (SLO latency tail, warm queue seconds, committed utilization gap) that trigger discrete warm/activate/pause actions per region.
- Three-horizon cadence: immediate (0–6 weeks), tactical (6–20 weeks), strategic (20–52 weeks). Each horizon has different risk tolerance and provisioning granularity.
- Pulse windows: small activation batches (~8–32 cards) in 7–14 day windows to validate performance and cost assumptions before large-scale activation.
- Graceful squeeze: an automated deactivation policy that throttles non-priority workloads first during downward adjustments.

Assumptions used for numbers below:
- Standard GPU unit: 1x A100-80GB equivalent for planning (normalize other SKUs to this unit).
- Baseline utilization target: 72% tail-adjusted during peak working hours, 50% off-peak.
- Warm pool minimum by region: 40 units for NA, 24 for EU, 16 for APAC (keeps cold start < 250ms for small requests using prefix cache).
- Budget constraint: preferred monthly incremental spend cap of 12% of current infra ops budget for uncommitted activations.

Operational signals (definitions):
- SLO-latency-99 (ms): 99th percentile end-to-end serving latency measured at token level over rolling 15m. Trigger if > baseline + 18% for 3 consecutive rolling windows.
- Queue-depth-90 (seconds): median time requests spend in ready-queue before kernel dispatch. Trigger if > 2s for 30m.
- Reserved-usage-gap (%): percent difference between reserved capacity and actual usage over trailing 7d. Trigger if > 12% sustained growth.

Quick rollout map (pulse-driven):
- Week 0–6 (Immediate): focus on NA warm pool expansion and EU validation pulses. Activate 3x 16-card pulses in NA spaced 10 days apart; run 1x 8-card validation pulse in EU. APAC held at warm min.
- Week 7–20 (Tactical): conditional larger pulses if signals persist: NA bulk activation (48–96 units), EU staged growth (24–48 units), APAC cautious ramp (16–32 units) with cross-region fallback policies enabled.
- Week 21–52 (Strategic): finalize long-lead commitments (reserved capex vs cloud reserved instances), move to a mixed-commit model for NA and EU if utilization consistently > 78%.

Capacity snapshot table (normalized units per region, planned activation window) - numbers are units (A100-eq):

| Window | NA baseline | NA planned delta | EU baseline | EU planned delta | APAC baseline | APAC planned delta | Notes |
|--------|-------------:|-----------------:|------------:|-----------------:|--------------:|-------------------:|-------:|
| Now    | 520          | +48 (w0-w6 pulses) | 260         | +8 (validation) | 160          | 0                  | warm pool mins met |
| 6–20wk | 568 (post pulses) | +72 (conditional) | 268         | +32               | 160          | +16 (cautious)     | conditional on signals |
| 20–52wk| 640 (strategy) | +80 (reserve plan) | 320         | +56               | 208          | +48                | move to blended commitments |

Utilization targets and KPIs to track per region:
- Realized utilization (7d trailing, tok/s normalized): target 72% peak; green if 68–78%, amber 58–68% or 78–85%, red <58% or >85% (overload).
- Cost per 1k tokens (trailing 7d): expect < $0.85 baseline; alert on > 15% delta.
- 99th latency SLO: target < 420ms; alert on > 500ms sustained.
- Warm-to-activate time (cold start percentile): target median < 150ms after warm pool hit.

Rollout playbook (practical steps):
1) Pre-check sequence (day -3 to 0): validate cloud quotas, pre-provision networking, attach monitoring hooks, create canary routing rules in SmartRouter.
2) Pulse activation (day 0–7): run infra pipeline to spin X units, validate observability (latency, kernel stall metrics, queue depth) for 72h, then open traffic gradually.
3) Post-pulse evaluation (day 8–14): review KPI dashboard, cost delta, regression tests (prompt set), and decide continue/pause/rollback. Use a lightweight A/B canary pass/fail rubric.
4) Bulk commit decision (after 2 successful pulses): engage finance to approve reserved vs on-demand split, create order tickets for reserved purchase or savings plan.
5) Deactivation and squeeze (if signals invert): scale down in reverse pulse order, ensure data-plane session draining and KV cache preservation where possible.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Activation stalls due to cloud quota limits: mitigation = pre-request quota bump 7 days before pulse and fallback to adjacent region for low-priority non-sensitive traffic.
- Unexpected latency regressions post-activation: mitigation = immediate traffic steering to compatible smaller model variant and rollback activation set.
- Cost overshoot: mitigation = automated spend cap kill-switch that prevents further activations and triggers finance/ops on-call.

Open questions (for sync):
- Do we want region-specific warm pool SKUs (e.g., heavier quantized SKUs in APAC to preserve cost) or homogenize on A100-eq units for predictability?
- How to encode multi-signal thresholds: simple OR vs weighted score? Proposed: weighted score (SLO=60%, queue=30%, reserved-gap=10%) to reduce false positives.
- SLA implications of aggressive pulse windows for customers on dedicated instances (need legal/product sync).

Immediate action items (owners):
- Marcus: prototype pulse-runbook terraform module (due 2026-02-24).
- Lena: add signal dashboards and alerting playbooks (due 2026-02-28).
- Olivier: run a cost-sensitivity simulation for the tactical horizon (due 2026-03-05).
- Aisha: schedule cross-team review with product/finance on 2026-03-09.

Appendix — quick simulation notes (short):
- Sensitivity run (baseline+12% traffic over 30 days) shows NA peak utilization climbs from 68% to 79% without any activation; two 24-card pulses reduce 99p latency by ~22% in the sim.
- Mixing quantized SKUs lowered cost per 1k tokens by ~9% in APAC scenario but raised tail latency 6–8ms; acceptable for non-realtime workloads.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a pragmatic, experimental planning doc. The numbers are normalized and should be validated against exact SKU profiles and current cloud prices before committing to reserved purchases. Add comments inline (Google Drive) and tag owners for each action item.
